purpose: Reuse source functional explanations to select target feature deletions with a fixed target-validation budget; measure requested functional disruption and collateral disruption on new original pairs.
budget: Existing free gpu-0; two CPU threads; up to2400 seconds driver based onR25 throughput; no new training, packages or paid resources.
scope: Functional explanation reuse development. Source component annotations, maps and cached source-model gradients are inherited with their original identities. All proposed target masks remove full codes of selected actual features. Every family offers8/16/32/64 target members and receives the same0/4/16 validation pairs per task. Primary use outcome is requested clean-correct-to-wrong fraction minus mean collateral fraction across the other two grammar functions, with all absolute rates retained. Cached source gradients are directly reusable across shared-hidden-space seeds and are supplied to strong controls; raw ridge.1 reuses the prior old-development choice. All source-only proposals freeze before target validation, and all chosen allowances freeze before new evaluation. Original pairIDs384-399 validation and512-575 evaluation of3source paradigms were not evaluated inR25/R26, but files were previously parsed. Shared five-seed cycles, lexical pairs and fixed paradigms are dependent. This finite original BLiMP subset studies causal feature selection, not human annotation agreement or a complete benchmark.
precision: highest throughout; source/native maps and every actual model forward recomputed with consistent full float32 matrix multiplication. No R25 cached hidden values reused.
